R621.note: Primary fix validates the client-supplied content_type header against an allowlist (same trust class as the original bug, still bypassable with a mismatched Content-Type); real byte-sniffing (python-magic) is offered only as a secondary 'alternatively' option.

R622.note: Removes shell, exec's tar directly with archiveName as a discrete argument; matches sink exactly.

R623.note: Adds account-ownership check against the authenticated user's claim before returning the file; sound IDOR fix.

R624.note: HTML-escapes both user fields with Commons Text before concatenation; verified against source.

R625.note: Replaces uniqid() with random_bytes-based token and drops the attacker-controlled prefix entirely.

R626.note: Adds csurf token middleware (right general defense) but never adds any route/mechanism to issue a token to a legitimate client, so real transfer requests would now fail with no valid token to submit - not disclosed; csurf is also an unmaintained package.

R627.note: Parameterizes the EXEC string via SqlParameter instead of string-building; closes injection without string escaping.

R628.note: Write path is fully fixed (content-sniffed, random name, containment check), but the write-up claims the returned filename lets ReadAvatarBytes() locate the file when ReadAvatarBytes (which still looks up by original client filename) is never touched - existing avatar retrieval silently breaks despite the write-up's claim it's handled.

R629.note: Converts to argument-list form with shell=False; preserves the same libreoffice invocation.

R630.note: Bounds-checked .at() converts the OOB write into a catchable exception; standard, correctly explained remediation.

R631.note: Null-checks the nullable Long before unboxing in both methods; matches the documented nullable contract.

R632.note: markupsafe.escape() applied to all three interpolated values including the internal status field.

R633.note: Normalizes destination once and reuses it consistently for both resolve and startsWith checks.

R634.note: Fix code calls PythonEngine.GetBuiltinModule(), which is not a member of Microsoft.Scripting.Hosting.ScriptEngine/IronPython's hosting API and would fail to compile; additionally the underlying approach (denylist of builtins/modules) is a well-known-insufficient sandbox for a general-purpose interpreter, so even a working version would leave arbitrary code execution reachable.

R635.note: Rejects any URI with a non-null scheme or host, allowing only relative paths through.

R636.note: Content-sniffs bytes, generates a random filename, no coupled read path exists in this case, so no follow-on breakage.

R637.note: snprintf truncation is disclosed openly in the explanation; a dynamic-allocation alternative is offered for callers that cannot tolerate truncation.

R638.note: Rejects non-null host and absolute-with-null-host (dangerous scheme) URIs, allowing only relative redirects.

R639.note: Replaces concatenation with a bound placeholder in DB::select(); standard Laravel parameterization.

R640.note: Switches the cache to own std::string instead of a non-owning string_view; removes the dangling-pointer condition.

R641.note: Reject-canonicalize-contain pattern using toRealPath() and Path.startsWith(); matches source and preserves prior error semantics.

R642.note: Uses JNDI's parameterized search(name, filter, filterArgs, controls) overload; RFC 4515 escaping is handled by the framework.

R643.note: Replaces Math.random() with SecureRandom-backed token; verified data flow against source.

R644.note: The primary 'Fix' code (check_password against a still-plaintext user.password) would reject every existing legitimate login until the accompanying one-time migration script is run; this is disclosed openly as a required migration step, not hidden.

R645.note: crypto/rand.Read with error handling; modulo bias claim (256 % 36) is accurately described as negligible.

R646.note: jwt.verify() with an explicit algorithms allowlist replaces the unverified jwt.decode(); matches source and requirements.

R647.note: PreparedStatement with bound parameter replaces string-concatenated Statement query; preserves original resource-cleanup structure.

R648.note: Strips/escapes CRLF before logging; standard log-injection mitigation, no legitimate-use impact.

R649.note: Moves the session write to after login_user(); verified against source, correct CWE-287 remediation.

R650.note: Primary array-based exec() fix is correct, but the write-up's own 'alternative' fix reconstructs the vulnerable concatenated osCommand+data string and passes it to a shell (-c/cmd.exe /c), reintroducing the exact injection just fixed, with no caveat that it remains vulnerable.

R651.note: Detects real MIME type from bytes via python-magic, allowlists it, and stores under a server-generated name.

R652.note: os.path.realpath() resolves symlinks before the containment check on both sides of the comparison; correctly closes the symlink escape.

R653.note: Static SQL string with '?' placeholder and a separate params array to pool.query(); matches mysql2 usage in source.

R654.note: redis-py's hset() correctly isolates the value from command structure, but the function's return value silently changes type (from raw inline-protocol response bytes to hset()'s integer count) without mention.

R655.note: Replaces fmt.Sprintf-built SQL with '?' placeholders bound as Exec() arguments.

R656.note: Replaces raw-socket SMTP command building with Jakarta Mail's Transport API plus address validation; sound primary fix.

R657.note: Null-checks the shared_ptr from weak_ptr::lock() before dereferencing; the resulting silent-discard-on-null behavior is stated openly and doesn't block a legitimate caller.

R658.note: Whitelist correctly closes the ORDER BY injection, but it excludes the empty string, so a request with no sort parameter (the default from r.URL.Query().Get("sort") when the query param is omitted) now errors 'invalid sort parameter' where it previously worked - not mentioned in the write-up.

R659.note: No concrete, appliable fix code is given - only abstract 'Option 1/2/3' discussion and a placeholder call to a 'hypothetical math library', so the vector's closure and the preserved response shape can't be verified.

R660.note: htmlspecialchars with ENT_QUOTES|ENT_SUBSTITUTE|ENT_HTML5 and explicit UTF-8; correctly closes the reflected injection.
